At about 10p.m. on 30-5-1939, a Japanese, dressed in

me asking to make a steel press bearing the design of an
anchor. (I cannot remember the characters of the press). We
settle the price for the press $18.00 and the Japanese left

we did not question him at all. On the 3-6-39, the Japanese
came to the shop and agreed on the production of a sample
shewn by us. Three days later, he came again and received
the ordered steel press after making the payment to us. The
steel press was made by the Hwa Fong Steel Press Shop, 45
South Tiendong Road. The above is my true statement.

SHANGHAI TIMES.

SEP 7 1938

Military Permits Are Basis
Of Defrauding Chinese

Group Of Chinese Racketeers Defraud Junk Masters
Of Various Sums On Pretext Of Providing Passes;
Fake Passes Discovered And Lead To Arrests

Two persons are being detained
by the First Special District Court,
in connection with a new line of
fraud in which numerous junkmen
were robbed of cash after being
promised by the firm, to which the
two accused belonged, to secure
Japanese military passes. It is
alleged that the firm known as the
"Shanghai Citizens Junk Industry
Friendship Club" has collected
about $2,000 from junkmen anxious
to get Japanese military permits
but after obtaining the money
officers of the firm vanished.

The leader of the latest racket
is alleged to be Ma Chung-hsiang,
manager of the firm solely engaged
in obtaining military passes. Junk-
men applying for permits from the
firm must pay procedure fees rang-
ing from $15 to $60. Many days
have passed, but no permits have
been issued. The registered junkmen
visited the firm which was located
at 792 Soochow Road many times,
but they were always disappointed.
On August 3 the firm was closed
without previous notice and no res-
ponsible officer of the company
could be found.

Last Sunday two assistants of the
closed firm, Sheng Hui-chi and
Chang Tze-hsiang, were met in the
street, near Nanking Road, by
several victimized junkmen who at
once reported the matter to the
police who arrested them and sent
them to the court. The hearing was
postponed pending further investi-
gations during which the police
expect to arrest the leader.

Faking Permits

Seventeen other persons are
being detained by the court on the
suspicion that they have counter-
feited Japanese military permits.
The crime was recently discovered
by Japanese garrison authorities in
Wusih where four villagers com-
ing from Shanghai were found to
be in possession of fake permits.
The origin of these forged docu-
ments was traced to Shanghai and
co-operating with the Municipal
Police the Japanese arrested the 17
accused, many of whom are con-
nected with transportation firms. It
is alleged that in their possession
many counterfeit permits were
found.

军用通行证成为
诈骗中国人的基础

一群中国勒索者借口提供通行证，
诈骗多位舢板船主各种金额；
发现假通行证并导致逮捕

第一特区法院正拘留两人，
涉及一种新的诈骗手段，许多舢板船主
在被这两名被告所属的公司承诺获取
日本军用通行证后，现金被骗走。据称，
这家名为“上海市民舢板业友谊会”的公司
从急于获得日本军用许可的舢板船主那里
收取了约2,000美元，但在拿到钱后，
公司职员便消失无踪。

据称，最新勒索团伙的头目是马忠祥，
该公司经理，专门从事获取军用通行证的业务。
向该公司申请许可的舢板船主必须支付
15至60美元不等的手续费。多日过去，
却未签发任何许可证。注册舢板船主多次
前往位于苏州路792号的公司，但总是失望而归。
8月3日，该公司在未事先通知的情况下关闭，
找不到公司的任何负责人。

上周日，几名受害的舢板船主在南京路附近
的街上遇到了已关闭公司的两名助手盛惠基
和张子祥，他们立即向警方报案，警方逮捕
了他们并将其送交法院。听证会推迟，以待
进一步调查，期间警方预计将逮捕头目。

伪造许可证

法院因涉嫌伪造日本军用许可证而拘留
了另外17人。这一罪行最近被无锡的日本
驻军当局发现，当时发现四名来自上海的
村民持有假许可证。这些伪造文件的来源
被追溯至上海，日本方面与工部局警务处
合作，逮捕了这17名被告，其中许多人与
运输公司有关联。据称，在他们身上发现了
许多伪造的许可证。

Made by D.C.I. HOWLETT Forwarded by C.D.I. GRUBB.

Sir,

At 4 p.m. on the 21st Feb. 1939 ... Umemoto of J.P.Office informed the undersigned that the Japanese Gendarmerie requested the assistance to effect the arrest of a gang of counterfeiters of Japanese Military passes.

At 6.40 p.m. Sergt-Major Hikichi and four other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie H.Q. came to C.D.H... and produced three counterfeit Japanese Military passes, which, Sergt-Major Hikichi stated, had been obtained by his agent from Chinese persons occupying a room No. 242 at the Sing Liu Say (新旅社) Lodging House, 79 Nanking Road.

These passes purporting to be issued by Japanese Military Police in Chekiang, had been sent for verification to the mentioned authority and same were found to be counterfeit ones. Also two specimens of the genuine passes were produced by Sergt-Major Hikichi.

Acting on instructions of C.D.I. Grubb, officer i/c C.I, the necessary assistance was rendered by J.D.C. Yamahara of the J.P.Office, D.S.I.s Soong Ping Tsung and Konovaloff and C.D.C. 267.

At 7 p.m. the room No.242 of the Sing Liu Say Lodging House was visited, but no persons were found in the room. A search of the room revealed one account book in which some remarks, relating to procuring of Japanese Military passes, was written thereon. On the door of the room was found a note

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

On the evening of 25-1-42 a verbal request was received from Japanese Gendarmerie for assistance to make 4 simultaneous raids at 8 a.m. Arrangements were made accordingly, and foreign and Chinese detectives were ordered to stand by.

The Gendarmerie failed to put in appearance at Headquarters and at about 9.20 a.m. 26-1-42 a telephone message was received from D.S. Yamahara requesting the attendance of a foreign detective at Kelly and Walsh Ltd.. Incorporated in Hongkong, 66 Nanking Road, as Gendarmerie were conducting a search therein.

D.I. Crighton attended and was informed by D.S. Yamahara that his party consisting of 10 persons, all of whom are Japanese professors seconded to the Gendarmerie, were conducting a search of the bookstore for literature considered to be of an anti-Japanese nature. D.S. Yamahara further explained to D.I.Crighton that 9 other parties were being despatched on a similar mission to other foreign bookstores.

In accordance with the usual custom the Japanese members of the S.M.P. who were detailed for this duty attended Bridge House to pick up the Gendarmerie parties and first bring them to Crime Branch Headquarters.

1942年1月25日晚，接到日本宪兵队的口头请求，要求协助在上午8点同时进行4次突击搜查。已相应做出安排，并命令外籍和华人侦探待命。

宪兵队未出现在总部，1942年1月26日上午9点20分左右，接到巡官山原（Yamahara，音译）的电话留言，请求派一名外籍侦探前往位于南京路66号的香港注册企业别发印书馆有限公司（Kelly and Walsh Ltd.），因为宪兵队正在那里进行搜查。

侦探督察克莱顿（Crighton）到场，山原巡官告知他，其一行10人均为借调至宪兵队的日本教授，正在搜查该书店中被认为具有反日性质的文献。山原巡官还向克莱顿侦探督察解释，另有9个分队正被派往其他外文书店执行类似任务。

按照惯例，被指派执行此项任务的工部局警务处日籍成员前往百老汇大厦（Bridge House）接载宪兵队分队，并首先将他们带至刑事科总部。
